primary.key: And if anyone of the idolaters seeketh thy protection (O Muhammad), then protect him so that he may hear the Word of Allah, and afterward convey him to his place of safety. That is because they are a folk who know not.
primary.s: After the order to slay the idolaters, the Prophet is told what to do when one of them asks for protection; al-Tabari, on 9:6, reads it as safety while he hears the Qur’an and, if he refuses Islam, safe passage home to his people.
primary.src: al-Tabari, Jāmiʿ al-bayān, on 9:6, the Arabic text of the Tarteel QUL library via spa5k/tafsir_api, commit 9ae590a (2026)

basis.words: فأمّنه حتى يسمع كلام الله وتتلوه عليه = ﴿ثم أبلغه مأمنه﴾ ، يقول: ثم رُدَّه بعد سماعه كلام الله إن هو أبَي أن يسلم، ولم يتعظ لما تلوته عليه من كلام الله فيؤمن = "إلى مأمنه"، يقول: إلى حيث يأمن منك وممن في طاعتك، حتى يلحق بداره وقومه من المشركين
basis.gloss: Grant him safety until he hears the word of God as you recite it to him; ‘then convey him to his place of safety’: send him back, after he has heard God’s word, if he refuses to become a Muslim and is not moved to believe by what you recited to him; ‘to his place of safety’: to where he is safe from you and from those who obey you, until he reaches his home and his people among the idolaters.

standby.key: If ye help him not, still Allah helped him when those who disbelieve drove him forth, the second of two; when they two were in the cave, when he said unto his comrade: Grieve not. Lo! Allah is with us.
standby.s: Rebuking believers who hang back from the call to fight, the chapter recalls the Prophet’s expulsion; Ibn Kathir, on 9:40, takes the comrade as Abu Bakr, afraid in the cave of Thawr that harm would reach the Prophet, who calmed him.
standby.src: Ibn Kathir, Tafsīr al-Qurʾān al-ʿAẓīm, on 9:40, the Arabic text of the Tarteel QUL library via spa5k/tafsir_api, commit 9ae590a (2026)

basis.words: فَخَرَجَ مِنْهُمْ هَارِبًا صُحْبَةَ صدِّيقه وَصَاحِبِهِ أَبِي بَكْرِ بْنِ أَبِي قُحَافَةَ، فَلَجَأَ إِلَى غَارِ ثَوْرٍ ثَلَاثَةَ أَيَّامٍ لِيَرْجِعَ الطَّلَبُ الَّذِينَ خَرَجُوا فِي آثَارِهِمْ، ثُمَّ يَسِيرَا نَحْوَ الْمَدِينَةِ، فَجَعَلَ أَبُو بَكْرٍ، رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ، يَجْزَعُ أَنْ يَطَّلع عَلَيْهِمْ أَحَدٌ، فَيَخْلُصَ إِلَى الرَّسُولِ، عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ مِنْهُمْ أَذًى، فَجَعَلَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ يُسَكِّنه ويَثبِّته
basis.gloss: He went out from them in flight, in the company of his truthful friend and companion Abu Bakr ibn Abi Quhafa, and took refuge in the cave of Thawr for three days, so that the pursuers who had set out on their tracks would turn back, and then the two would travel on towards Medina; and Abu Bakr began to fear that someone would come upon them and that harm from them would reach the Messenger, so the Prophet set about calming and steadying him.

primary.key: And the believers should not all go out to fight. Of every troop of them, a party only should go forth, that they (who are left behind) may gain sound knowledge in religion, and that they may warn their folk when they return to them, so that they may beware.
primary.s: In a chapter that commands fighting and condemns staying behind, the believers learn who must march; al-Tabari, on 9:121 to 9:122, takes the understanding as gained by the party that marches, not by those who stay, from seeing God’s victory for the believers.
primary.src: al-Tabari, Jāmiʿ al-bayān, on 9:121 to 9:122, the Arabic text of the Tarteel QUL library via spa5k/tafsir_api, commit 9ae590a (2026)

basis.words: فإن أولى الأقوال في ذلك بالصواب، قولُ من قال: ليتفقه الطائفة النافرة بما تعاين من نصر الله أهلَ دينه وأصحابَ رسوله، على أهل عداوته والكفر به … فإن قال قائل: وما تنكر أن يكون معناه: ليتفقه المتخلِّفون في الدين؟ قيل: ننكر ذلك لاستحالته.
basis.gloss: The most correct of the views on this is the saying of whoever said: let the party that marches out gain understanding by what it witnesses of God’s giving victory to the people of His religion and the companions of His Messenger over those hostile to Him and disbelieving in Him ... If someone asks, why do you reject that it means ‘so that those who stay behind may gain understanding in religion’, the answer is: we reject it because it is impossible.

standby.key: Not unto the weak nor unto the sick nor unto those who can find naught to spend is any fault (to be imputed though they stay at home) if they are true to Allah and His messenger. Not unto the good is there any road (of blame).
standby.s: In a chapter condemning those who stayed back from fighting, the verse names who is excused; Ibn Kathir, on 9:91 to 9:93, takes the excuse as holding provided those who stay are sincere and neither spread alarm nor hold others back.
standby.src: Ibn Kathir, Tafsīr al-Qurʾān al-ʿAẓīm, on 9:91 to 9:93, the Arabic text of the Tarteel QUL library via spa5k/tafsir_api, commit 9ae590a (2026)

basis.words: ثُمَّ بَيَّنَ تَعَالَى الْأَعْذَارَ الَّتِي لَا حَرَج عَلَى مَنْ قَعَدَ فِيهَا عَنِ الْقِتَالِ … فَلَيْسَ عَلَى هَؤُلَاءِ حَرَج إِذَا قَعَدُوا وَنَصَحُوا فِي حَالِ قُعُودِهِمْ، وَلَمْ يُرْجِفُوا بِالنَّاسِ، وَلَمْ يُثَبِّطوهم، وَهُمْ مُحْسِنُونَ فِي حَالِهِمْ هَذَا
basis.gloss: Then God set out the excuses for which there is no blame on one who stays back from fighting ... so there is no blame on these if they stay back and are sincere while they stay, and do not spread alarm among the people or hold them back; they are doing good in this state of theirs.
